acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Fae family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Fae Knight, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Glass-Antler Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Human-sized Fae Knight with stained-glass wings, antlers of woven branches, leaf-and-bark armor, and an unnervingly still face.
Signature mechanic: False Rose Path: one antler frames a colored wing pane, projecting three apparent thrust lanes while only the pane without an antler reflection carries the leaf-armored charge.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a refractive lane controller whose stained-glass wings and branch antlers cast conflicting route signs.
constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity wild-wood imagery, ordinary leaf, bark, and branches, glowing pollen or glowing motes, dew, stained glass, and T5 reality bending remain source-supported material, ornament, light, and perceptual behavior—not retired Wood affinity or any current elemental affinity.
Petals, spider silk, moth wing, thorn, garland, antlers, masks, and restrained seasonal color retain crisp physical or uncanny boundaries without elemental substitution.
counterplay: Take the pane with no antler reflection and strike the rigid wing rib after the charge passes. Affinity signal: The established wing root, petal seam, antler reflection, mask edge, or season-crown break remains readable.
forbiddenTreatments: Treating ordinary plants, pollen light, dew, or stained glass as affinity evidence
identityInvariants: A slender weightless-looking silhouette retains layered wings while scale, head growth, and proportion change only at explicit tiers.
Spring green, petal pink, dusk violet, moth iridescence, and bounded gold pollen light remain source palette rather than affinity evidence.
Living leaf, petal, spider silk, stained glass, bark, dew, and moth wing remain discrete ordinary or uncanny materials.
Wing complexity and subtly wrong beauty escalate from a palm sprite to a sovereign whose geometry bends the surrounding frame.
telegraph: The unnervingly still face turns last, one woven antler crosses a stained-glass pane, and two reflected lanes brighten.
